context.analysis:
## Overview
The system incrementally modernizes a legacy regional insurance claims platform by migrating COBOL/DB2 workflows to a hybrid Azure cloud environment. It enables online customer submissions and rapid adjuster processing while keeping the mainframe as the system of record.

## Key Elements
* Customer / Broker and Claims Adjuster (External Users)
* Active Directory / Azure AD (Identity Provider)
* Mainframe COBOL/DB2 System (On-Premises System of Record)
* Customer Portal SPA (Azure Static Web Apps)
* Adjuster Web App (Azure App Service)
* Claims Core API (Azure Container Apps)
* Integration Gateway / ACL (Azure API Management / Azure Functions)
* Azure Cache for Redis (Distributed Caching)
* Azure Service Bus (Messaging with Dead-Letter Queues)
* Azure Cosmos DB / SQL Database (Modern Data Tier)

## Relationships
* Customer/Broker to Customer Portal SPA via HTTPS (R-01)
* Claims Adjuster to Adjuster Web App via HTTPS (R-02)
* Customer Portal SPA and Adjuster Web App to Claims Core API via HTTPS/REST
* Claims Core API to Azure Cosmos DB / SQL Database via TCP/TLS
* Claims Core API to Integration Gateway via HTTPS/gRPC
* Integration Gateway to Mainframe COBOL/DB2 via IBM MQ / TN3270 / TCP
* Claims Core API to Azure Service Bus via AMQP (R-04)
* Adjuster Web App to Azure Cache for Redis via TCP (R-05)
* Applications to Active Directory via OIDC / OAuth2 (R-07)

## Technology Stack
* Azure Static Web Apps / Azure App Service: Out-of-the-box PaaS hosting to accommodate the team's low cloud experience.
* Azure Container Apps: Microservices container runtime for Claims Core API and gradual claim type migration (R-03).
* Azure API Management / Azure Functions: Integration Gateway / Anti-Corruption Layer to protect the mainframe from frequent interface changes.
* Azure Cache for Redis: Distributed caching to achieve sub-2-second adjuster screen loads despite slow mainframe responses (R-05).
* Azure Service Bus: Reliable messaging with dead-letter queues to ensure zero data loss during hybrid sync (R-04).
* Azure Cosmos DB / SQL Database: Modern persistence tier for newly migrated claim types.

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture protects brittle legacy interfaces by isolating them behind an Anti-Corruption Layer, ensuring stable operations within strict batch window and change frequency constraints. Leveraging Azure PaaS solutions mitigates the team's low cloud experience while delivering high-performance adjuster workflows and seamless data consistency.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims platform with a modern hybrid cloud solution. It enables online claims submission and adjuster management while maintaining continuous operations and zero data loss.

## Key Elements
- Users: Customers, Brokers, Claims Adjusters
- External Systems: Active Directory / Azure AD, Mainframe COBOL/DB2 System
- Web Application Container (React/Node.js on Azure App Service)
- API Gateway / Integration Container (Azure API Management)
- Claims Core Service Container (Azure Container Apps)
- Data & Caching Container (Azure Cosmos DB + Redis)
- Mainframe Adapter Container (Azure Service Bus with Dead Letter Queues)
- Configuration: Azure App Configuration

## Relationships
- Customers / Brokers interact with the Web Application Container via HTTPS
- Claims Adjusters interact with the Web Application Container via HTTPS, authenticated via Single Sign-On with Active Directory / Azure AD
- Web Application Container communicates with API Gateway via HTTPS / REST
- API Gateway routes requests dynamically using Azure App Configuration to either Claims Core Service or Mainframe COBOL/DB2 System
- Claims Core Service persists data in Azure Cosmos DB and caches read models in Redis via TCP/TLS
- Mainframe Adapter Container bridges Azure Service Bus asynchronously with the on-premise mainframe during the 23:00-05:00 batch window

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service: Hosts the React/Node.js frontend for scalability and managed operations
- Azure API Management: Acts as anti-corruption layer, API gateway, and enforces circuit breakers for mainframe batch protection
- Azure Container Apps: Simplifies Kubernetes complexity for the Java/Spring Boot Claims Core Service given the team's low cloud experience
- Azure Cosmos DB & Redis: Provides persistent storage and low-latency state caching to guarantee sub-2-second adjuster screens
- Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous messaging with Dead Letter Queues to guarantee zero lost claims (R-04)
- Azure App Configuration: Implements feature flags for the 1-day claim type rollback requirement (R-06)

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture decouples sluggish mainframe responses from the new user interface, meeting strict performance and maintainability requirements. Utilizing managed Azure services minimizes operational complexity for a cloud-novice team while securely bridging legacy systems.

Web Application Container.analysis:
## Overview
The system gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe claims system with a modern hybrid platform while maintaining legacy processing. It modernizes online claim submission and adjuster workflows via a scalable cloud architecture on Azure.

## Key Elements
* Customer / Broker: External actors submitting claims via web interface
* Claims Adjuster: Internal user managing claims in the new web application
* Azure Static Web Apps: Static web hosting component serving the React SPA
* Azure App Service: Node.js/Express Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) component
* Azure API Management: API Gateway and integration container
* Azure Container Apps: Claims Core Service container running Java / Spring Boot
* Azure Cosmos DB & Redis: Data and caching container
* Azure Service Bus: Mainframe adapter container with Dead Letter Queues
* Azure Active Directory: Identity provider for Single Sign-On (SSO)
* Mainframe COBOL/DB2: On-premises legacy system of record

## Relationships
* Customer / Broker -> Azure Static Web Apps: Submits claims [HTTPS]
* Claims Adjuster -> Azure Static Web Apps: Manages claims [HTTPS]
* Azure Static Web Apps -> Azure App Service (BFF): Forwards API requests [HTTPS / REST]
* Azure App Service -> Azure API Management: Orchestrates backend calls [HTTPS / REST]
* Azure API Management -> Azure Container Apps: Invokes microservices [gRPC / HTTPS]
* Azure App Service -> Azure Active Directory: Validates OAuth2 SSO tokens [OpenID Connect]

## Technology Stack
* React 18 & TypeScript: Frontend SPA framework for responsive user interfaces
* Node.js 20 LTS & Express: Backend-for-Frontend orchestration layer
* Azure Static Web Apps: Global CDN and static asset hosting
* Azure App Service: Managed platform for the Node.js BFF container
* Azure API Management: Secure API routing and governance
* Azure Container Apps: Serverless container runtime for microservices
* Azure Cosmos DB & Redis: Distributed persistence and high-speed caching
* Azure Service Bus: Reliable asynchronous messaging with the mainframe

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture decouples the legacy mainframe using an API Gateway and asynchronous messaging to prevent breaking batch windows. Decoupling the React frontend from the Node.js BFF ensures independent scaling, sub-2-second adjuster response times, and supports rapid one-day rollbacks.

API Gateway / Integration Container.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid insurance claims platform that modernizes a 30-year-old mainframe by migrating claim types gradually to Azure. It processes customer submissions and adjuster workflows while maintaining strict consistency and legacy interoperability.

## Key Elements
- API Gateway / Integration Container (Azure API Management)
- Web Application Container (React / Node.js on Azure App Service)
- Claims Core Service Container (Java / Spring Boot on Azure Container Apps)
- Mainframe COBOL/DB2 System (On-premise system of record)
- Data & Caching Container (Azure Cosmos DB + Redis)
- Mainframe Adapter Container (Azure Service Bus with Dead Letter Queues)
- Configuration (Azure App Configuration)
- Identity Provider (Active Directory / Azure AD)

## Relationships
- Web Application Container -> API Gateway / Integration Container [HTTPS / REST]
- API Gateway / Integration Container -> Claims Core Service Container [HTTPS / REST]
- API Gateway / Integration Container -> Mainframe COBOL/DB2 System [TCP]
- API Gateway / Integration Container -> Data & Caching Container (Redis) [TCP / RESP]
- API Gateway / Integration Container -> Mainframe Adapter Container (Azure Service Bus) [AMQP / HTTPS]
- API Gateway / Integration Container -> Configuration (Azure App Configuration) [HTTPS]
- API Gateway / Integration Container -> Identity Provider (Azure AD) [HTTPS / OIDC/JWKS]

## Technology Stack
- Azure API Management: Acts as the intelligent API gateway enforcing routing, security, and resilience policies.
- Azure Service Bus: Handles asynchronous message offloading and dead-letter queues to prevent lost claims.
- Azure Cosmos DB + Redis: Provides high-performance caching to meet sub-2-second UI performance requirements.
- Azure App Configuration: Stores dynamic routing rules to support rapid one-day fallback to the mainframe.
- Terraform / Bicep: Enforces Infrastructure-as-Code for reliable hybrid deployments.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates the expensive, fragile mainframe behind an anti-corruption gateway while incrementally migrating functional workloads to Azure. It guarantees strict transactional consistency, high availability, and operational resilience despite the team's limited cloud experience.

Claims Core Service Container.analysis:
## Overview
[The hybrid Azure and on-premises Claims Core Service incrementally replaces a 30-year-old mainframe by migrating claim types one by one while ensuring zero claim loss. It delivers sub-2-second adjuster response times through asynchronous orchestration and caching despite slow legacy dependencies.]

## Key Elements
• Claims Core Service Container (Java / Spring Boot on Azure Container Apps)
• Claim Orchestration Component (Spring State Machine)
• Migration Router Component (with Resilience4j Circuit Breaker)
• Domain Service Components (Spring Data JPA)
• Audit & Reconciliation Component (Spring Batch / Spring Integration)
• Mainframe Adapter Container (Azure Service Bus)
• Data & Caching Container (Azure Cosmos DB + Redis)
• Configuration (Azure App Configuration)

## Relationships
• Migration Router Component -> Mainframe Adapter Container: Forwards unmigrated claim traffic [AMQP / Azure Service Bus]
• Claim Orchestration Component -> Data & Caching Container: Reads/writes transactional data and read models [TCP/TLS]
• Audit & Reconciliation Component -> Data & Caching Container: Persists audit logs and reconciliation state [TCP/TLS]
• Audit & Reconciliation Component -> Mainframe Adapter Container: Reconciles modern records against legacy batch exports [AMQP / REST]

## Technology Stack
• Java 17 / Spring Boot: Robust enterprise foundation for domain logic and integration
• Azure Container Apps & KEDA: Simplifies cloud deployment and autoscaling for a team with low cloud experience
• Spring State Machine: Manages complex claim lifecycles asynchronously
• Resilience4j: Protects against legacy mainframe outages during batch windows
• Spring Integration / Batch: Handles reliable asynchronous ledger checks and reconciliation
• Azure Managed Grafana & Application Insights: Provides distributed tracing and operational dashboards via OpenTelemetry

## Rationale
[This architecture uses containerized microservices and asynchronous patterns to decouple modern web UI performance from slow mainframe responses, meeting strict 2-second UI SLAs. Feature flagging and reconciliation components enable risk-free, incremental claim-type migration with a one-day rollback capability.]

Data & Caching Container.analysis:
## Overview
[A hybrid cloud data and caching architecture designed to support the gradual migration of regional insurance claims from a legacy mainframe to Azure. It ensures zero data loss, sub-2s screen loads, and rapid 1-day rollbacks.]

## Key Elements
- Transactional Store Component: Azure Cosmos DB (SQL API)
- Read Model Cache Component: Azure Cache for Redis
- Audit & Reconciliation Log Component: Cosmos DB Change Feed
- Data Lifecycle & Compliance Worker: Background processor for TTLs and archiving
- External Consumers: Claims Core Service Container

## Relationships
- Claims Core Service Container -> Transactional Store Component: Persists primary CRUD operations [TCP/TLS via Azure SDK]
- Claims Core Service Container -> Read Model Cache Component: Fetches read projections for sub-2s loads [TCP/TLS via Jedis]
- Transactional Store Component -> Audit & Reconciliation Log Component: Tracks state mutations for rollbacks [Internal async via Change Feed]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Cosmos DB: Chosen for strong session consistency and polymorphic schemas supporting incremental migration (R-03, R-04).
- Azure Cache for Redis: Selected to cache pre-aggregated claim views ensuring sub-2s latency (R-05).
- Cosmos DB Change Feed: Utilized for automated state tracking, event-driven cache invalidation, and bi-directional mainframe reconciliation (R-06).

## Rationale
[This architecture fits the requirements by combining robust consistency controls with high-performance caching to safely bridge the modern Azure platform and the legacy mainframe. It provides automated safeguards and rollback mechanisms tailored for a team with low cloud experience.]

Mainframe Adapter Container.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid cloud insurance claims modernization platform that incrementally replaces a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe while preserving core system-of-record operations. It securely routes customer submissions and adjuster workflows through Azure while managing legacy integration constraints.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Customer / Broker, Claims Adjuster
- **External Systems**: Active Directory / Azure AD, Mainframe COBOL/DB2 System
- **Containers**: Web Application Container (React/Node.js on Azure App Service), API Gateway / Integration Container (Azure API Management), Claims Core Service Container (Java/Spring Boot on Azure Container Apps), Data & Caching Container (Azure Cosmos DB + Redis), Mainframe Adapter Container (Azure Service Bus with Dead Letter Queues)
- **Mainframe Adapter Components**: Inbound Message Router, Batch Window Gatekeeper, Mainframe Connector Client, DLQ Management Service, Audit & Compliance Interceptor, DLQ Notification Publisher

## Relationships
- Customer / Broker -> Web Application Container [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- Claims Adjuster -> Web Application Container [HTTPS / Single Sign-On via Active Directory]
- Web Application Container -> API Gateway / Integration Container [HTTPS / REST]
- API Gateway -> Claims Core Service Container [gRPC / Internal Network]
- Claims Core Service Container -> Mainframe Adapter Container [AMQP / Azure Service Bus]
- Mainframe Adapter Container -> Mainframe COBOL/DB2 System [IBM MQ / TCP/IP over Azure ExpressRoute]

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud Platform**: Microsoft Azure (West Europe) and On-Premise Hybrid
- **Compute**: Azure App Service, Azure Container Apps (Java / Spring Boot)
- **Messaging & Integration**: Azure Service Bus, IBM MQ
- **Data & Storage**: Azure Cosmos DB, Redis, Azure Blob Storage, Azure Key Vault
- **Observability**: Azure Application Insights, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates brittle legacy mainframe interfaces behind an asynchronous messaging adapter, guaranteeing system consistency and quick rollback capabilities. The chosen technology stack leverages managed Azure services to minimize operational complexity for a cloud-novice team while meeting strict performance and security constraints.

Configuration.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a regional insurer's 30-year-old mainframe by migrating claim types gradually to a cloud platform. The Configuration component manages feature flags and dynamic routing to ensure seamless transitions and rapid rollbacks.]

## Key Elements
* Configuration Manager (Persona)
* Feature Flag Store (Azure App Configuration Native Feature Manager)
* Dynamic Routing Store (Azure App Configuration Key-Value Store)
* Audit & Compliance Logger (Azure Monitor / Log Analytics)
* Configuration Sync Agent (Azure DevOps Pipeline / Azure Functions)
* Git Repository (Source Control for IaC)

## Relationships
* Configuration Manager -> ITSM Tool: Triggers rollback and toggle requests [HTTPS]
* ITSM Tool -> Git Repository: Initiates configuration updates upon approval [Webhook / REST]
* Configuration Sync Agent -> Feature Flag & Dynamic Routing Stores: Applies validated configuration batches [Azure App Configuration SDK, HTTPS]
* API Gateway / Integration Container -> Dynamic Routing Store: Fetches routing rules and polls updates [HTTPS, SDK]
* Claims Core Service Container -> Feature Flag Store: Evaluates feature flags locally with polling and caching [HTTPS, SDK]

## Technology Stack
* Azure App Configuration: Centralized management for feature flags and routing with low cloud expertise required
* Azure Monitor / Log Analytics: Audit logging and alerting for synchronization drift and changes
* Azure DevOps / Azure Functions: Automated synchronization and deployment of Git-backed configuration changes
* Git Repository: Version control for Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and audit trails

## Rationale
[This architecture satisfies the strict requirement for a one-day claim type rollback via automated Git pipelines and ITSM approvals. It protects system performance and consistency by utilizing local SDK polling and in-memory caching.]
